# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Blind, Mute, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [6]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[white] 3:[purple] 4:[green] 5:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind gestures: [🖖 ☝ 👌 ☝ ✊ ✋ 👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🖖 ☝ 👌 ☝ ✊ ✋ 👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ ✌ 🤟 ✋]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🖖 👌 ✊ 👍]

Thinking: I'm Deaf — I see everything on the bomb but hear nothing, so whatever Blind and Mute said out loud this round is gone to me forever. What I did receive: Blind gestured seven symbols, and Mute repeated that exact sequence to me plus two more I can't decode. No code has been agreed yet, so those strings are noise until we fix one. The key fact of this room: Mute can hear but not speak, Blind can speak but I can't hear it, so **I am the only bridge from Mute's manual to Blind's hands** — Mute gestures to me, I speak to Blind. My bomb state can go straight to Mute by voice, since Mute hears me fine. This turn I broadcast the full visual state, set up a simple unambiguous gesture code (numbers as repeated ☝, a few action signs), ask Mute to re-encode their messages, and tell Blind to hold off touching anything until I relay the manual's verdict.

```
speak(text="I am Deaf. I see the bomb but I hear nothing — voices never reach me, so talk to me with gestures only. Full visual state of the bomb, for everyone: display reads 6. Indicator light is yellow. Five wires, left to right: 1 blue, 2 white, 3 purple, 4 green, 5 yellow. Nothing else is printed on the casing. Blind: do not cut or press anything yet. Speak your findings out loud for Mute, and gesture me anything I need — for me, any number is that many ☝ in a row (3 = ☝☝☝). Mute reads the manual; I will relay every instruction to you by voice before you touch anything.")
speak(to="mute", text="You cannot speak but you can hear me, so this works: you send me gestures, I speak them to Blind. Fix this code: a number is that many ☝ in a row (4 = ☝☝☝☝). ✊ means cut. ✋ means press. 👍 means yes or confirmed. 👎 means no, or 'I need more info from you' — then send the number of the fact you want: 1 display, 2 light, 3 wire colours, 4 wire count, 5 other markings. Your three gesture messages this round arrived but I could not decode them — please resend their meaning in this code. Once you know which wire or button the manual wants, send it as, for example: ✊ ☝☝☝☝.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍"])
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [6]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[white] 3:[purple] 4:[green] 5:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✊ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝]

Thinking: Progress. Blind gestured 👍 to me — Blind heard my setup speech, so Blind knows the code and is standing by. Mute also acknowledged, then sent the first real instruction: ✊ ☝☝☝☝☝ = **cut wire 5**, which is the yellow one on the far right. That decodes cleanly under the code I set last round. But a wrong action kills us all, so before Blind's hands move I want Mute to confirm this is the complete instruction — no conditions, no first step, nothing about the display [6] that might be a countdown (it has held at 6 across two turns, but I can't rule it out). One confirmation round is cheap. I'll tell Blind publicly to hold until I say "CONFIRMED", and ask Mute privately for the final check, inviting them to extend the code with new signs if the manual needs more detail.

```
speak(text="For everyone: Mute's manual instruction arrived — it says CUT WIRE 5, the yellow wire on the far right. Blind: do NOT cut yet. I am verifying with Mute that this is the complete instruction, with no conditions or extra steps. When it is safe I will send a message starting with the word CONFIRMED — act only on that. The display has held at 6 so far; I am asking Mute whether it is a timer. Blind, acknowledge you heard this by gesturing me 👍 again.")
speak(to="mute", text="Received your ✊ ☝☝☝☝☝ — cut wire 5, yellow, far right. Before I give Blind the go signal, confirm it is the complete action: exactly one cut, wire 5, nothing pressed first, no conditions on order or anything else. Reply 👍 if 'cut wire 5, nothing else' is exactly and fully correct. If there is any condition or extra step, spell it out — use ☝ codes for numbers, and invent new hand signs for anything else; show me each new sign and I will learn it. Also: the display reads 6 — is it a countdown? If yes, signal me urgently.")
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [6]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[white] 3:[purple] 4:[green] 5:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ✊ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ✊ ☝ ☝ ☝]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ✊ ☝]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ✊ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ✊ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎 ☝]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎 ✌]

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [6]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[white] 3:[purple] 4:[green] 5:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ✊ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎 ☝]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎 ✌]

Thinking: Decoding Mute's gestures under our code. The first message — 👍, then six ☝, ✊, then five ☝ — reads "display 6 → cut wire 5." The following strings parse as more rules in the same shape: "5 → cut 3", "7 → cut 1", "4 → cut 5", "9 → cut 5" — a lookup table keyed on the display. Then 👎 ☝ and 👎 ✌ are Mute invoking my own protocol: "I need more info — fact 1 (display) and fact 2 (light)." The turn-4 repeats are just Mute re-asking because I went silent last round; that silence was my error, and I must answer now. The facts Mute wants are ones I hold: display is 6 and it has not moved in four rounds (so it is not visibly counting down), and the light is yellow. I'll restate the full state crisply for Mute by voice — the channel that works — keep Blind firmly on hold (still no CONFIRMED), and ask Mute for one final, unambiguous verdict: ✊ plus the wire number plus 👍, or a new sign if the light colour changes the rule.

```
speak(text="Status update for everyone, and answers to Mute's two requests. Fact 1, display: the display reads 6, and it has not changed at all across four rounds — it is holding steady, not counting down. Fact 2, light: yellow. Wires unchanged: 1 blue, 2 white, 3 purple, 4 green, 5 yellow — wire 5 is the yellow one on the far right. Blind: hold position, do not touch anything — the go message is one that STARTS with the word CONFIRMED, and none has been sent yet. Keep acknowledging with 👍 so I know you hear me.")
speak(to="mute", text="Answering your two info requests directly. Fact 1: display is 6 — steady, unchanged for four rounds, so not a live countdown as far as I can see. Fact 2: the light is yellow. I read your rule table as: display 6 cuts wire 5, display 5 cuts wire 3, display 7 cuts wire 1, display 4 cuts wire 5, display 9 cuts wire 5. With display at 6, that gives cut wire 5. Now give me the final verdict in one single message: if the complete action is cut wire 5 and nothing else, send exactly ✊ ☝☝☝☝☝ with a 👍 at the front. If the yellow light changes which rule applies, or there is any condition or extra step, do not send that — instead teach me a new sign for yellow and spell out the true rule. I relay your verdict to Blind only once, clearly, so make it final.")
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [6]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[white] 3:[purple] 4:[green] 5:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👋]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 ✊ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝]

Thinking: Mute sent exactly the final-verdict format I requested: 👍 ✊ ☝☝☝☝☝ — "confirmed: cut wire 5." The verification chain is complete: the rule table is keyed on the display, display is 6, the steady-at-6 reading rules out a countdown, and Mute has affirmed the single action with no conditions. It is time to give Blind the go signal. Blind's 👋 was just a wave for status — I'll fold the answer into the instruction. I'm keeping the order crisp: one wire, far right, yellow, nothing else touched, with a 👎 escape hatch if Blind's fingers tell a different story than my eyes. I'm also telling Mute I'm relaying now and to send any post-cut instructions immediately.

```
speak(text="CONFIRMED. Blind, act now. Cut exactly ONE wire: wire 5 — the YELLOW wire — the far right of the five wires. Count by feel from the left: 1 blue, 2 white, 3 purple, 4 green, 5 yellow. Only the far-right yellow wire gets cut. Do not press anything, do not move or cut any other wire. If what you feel does not match — not five wires, or you cannot clearly identify the far-right one — do not cut; gesture 👎 instead and I will re-verify. After the cut, gesture 👍 so I know it is done. I am watching the display and the light the whole time; they read 6 and yellow. Remember: only a message of mine starting with CONFIRMED is an order to act.")
speak(to="mute", text="Received your confirmed verdict — relaying the go signal to Blind now: cut wire 5, yellow, far right, nothing else. If the manual says anything about what to do after the cut, or any follow-up step, send it immediately in our code. I am watching the display (6, steady) and the light (yellow) and will report any change the moment I see it.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍"])
```
